## TRA Timeline

#### Up-C IPO and TRA execution

- 2006-12-15: Form-of TRA filed as Exhibit 10.3 to S-1/A Amendment No. 2
- 2007-02-05: TRA entered into at IPO close, 85% of cash tax savings to HFF Holdings, LLC

#### Up-C collapse

- 2012-08-31: HFF Holdings exchanges all remaining Operating Partnership units for HFF Class A stock; TRA continues in force because basis step-ups generated by past exchanges continue to amortize

#### JLL acquisition (TRA assumed, not terminated)

- 2019-03-18: JLL signs definitive merger agreement; DEFM14A later describes TRA as remaining in force with $50.3M estimated future payments and $97.3M cumulative paid through Q1 2019
- 2019-07-01: Merger closes; TRA assumed by surviving HFF subsidiary of JLL; Morgan Stanley's fairness opinion deducts the TRA's present value (~$40M) from enterprise value to equity value
- 2019-07: HFF deregisters; no further EDGAR filings under HFF CIK

## Explanation

HFF executed a Tax Receivable Agreement at its February 2007 Up-C IPO, obligating the public company to pay 85% of the cash tax savings from Section 754 basis step-ups (on exchanges of Operating Partnership units by HFF Holdings, LLC) to HFF Holdings as sole counterparty. By August 2012 HFF Holdings had fully exchanged out of the Operating Partnerships, completing an Up-C collapse, but the TRA continued because the already-realized basis step-ups produced ongoing amortization deductions. At the July 2019 Jones Lang LaSalle acquisition, the TRA was assumed rather than terminated: the DEFM14A and pro forma balance sheet describe it as a continuing obligation of the surviving HFF subsidiary, Morgan Stanley deducted its present value (~$40M) in the equity valuation, and no termination amendment or buyout was filed. HFF deregistered shortly after close, so the TRA's post-July-2019 trajectory is not visible from HFF's own filings; status is recorded as Unknown pending a sweep of JLL's filings. See `contract_log.md` for the full filing-by-filing record.
